Light fixtures: bulbs and the relay that feeds them, one light on the dashboard. Saving restarts Moli.
A ceiling light of three bulbs behind a connected switch, for instance. Orders go to the bulbs; the relay only cuts when none answers, and comes back by itself when the light is switched on.
Optional: the connected switch that cuts the bulbs’ power. Moli switches it back on when the light is switched on.
Choose bulbs, a relay, or both.
These bulbs are not answering now: a switch probably cuts them. With their relay, they become a light switched back on with one touch.

A bulb cut at the wall no longer answers: the dashboard says it is “cut at the switch”. A fixture gathers its bulbs and its relay: one button, which switches the relay back on if needed, and a colour per bulb.
Lights of several rooms set to a mood in one gesture, and the lights that follow the time of day. Saving restarts Moli.
A scene says, light by light, off or a mood; a light it does not name is left alone.
A wall button or an automation goes from one scene to the next; with no scene ticked, all of them are in it.
Orders sent after the lights: a TV’s Ambilight, a plug…
A scene has at least one light.
A light switched on takes the white and level of the hour, then follows them. Moli never switches anything on by itself; a light set by hand is no longer followed until it is switched off.

Between two times, the white and the level glide from one to the other.

Where and when an agent (Moli, a voice, an AI assistant, a script) must ask a person, and what wants the code. Nothing is protected by default. Saving restarts Moli.
Who commands from the dashboard opened without a code.
The household commands without a code (home network and recognized people), except in protected rooms where the code is asked.
Every command needs a session opened with the code; everything else (agents, scripts, dashboard without code) waits for a person. Approved automations go on.
An agent asks a person there; on the dashboard, the code is asked. For bedrooms, for instance.
No known room: set the rooms first.

No room ticked: the whole house.
Orders that want the code every time, even with an open session (disarming the alarm). Only an approved automation goes without; a scene, the heating or load shedding cannot carry them.

The values concerned; none ticked: all of them.
